notice: Illustrative preview data for design and deployment testing. These are not published GrepSignal findings.

signals.title: The web is becoming agent-native
signals.summary: WebMCP, browser agents, and machine-operable interfaces are converging. The important change is not another protocol; it is that websites are beginning to expose actions for agents rather than only pixels for humans.
signals.why_it_matters: Agent traffic may become a distribution channel of its own.
signals.watch_next: Major SaaS vendors exposing stable machine-operable actions.

signals.title: Coding agents are shifting from interaction to delegation
signals.summary: Tooling is increasingly optimized for longer autonomous work, persistent context, and fewer human checkpoints. The unit of work is drifting from ‘answer this’ toward ‘own this task until review.’
signals.why_it_matters: Workflow design may matter more than single-turn benchmark gains.
signals.second_order_effect: longer autonomy → fewer handoffs → new review bottlenecks
signals.watch_next: Reliability over multi-hour tasks and recovery after failures.

signals.title: Local inference economics keep improving — but not uniformly
signals.summary: Better quantization and stronger mid-size models can reduce local serving cost while frontier-model capability also becomes cheaper. The build-vs-buy boundary keeps moving.
signals.why_it_matters: Hardware purchases age faster as the intelligence-per-dollar curve moves.
signals.second_order_effect: cheaper inference → more viable workloads → thinner product moats
signals.watch_next: Quality-per-dollar on real agent and BI workloads, not only benchmarks.
